tasks.name: lints-what-it-writes
tasks.prompt: The goal is settled, write the spec to docs/specs/export.md: the two accountants download the rows they currently see on the reports page as a CSV file. File name reports-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. Same rows and order as on screen after filtering. Button disabled when there are no rows. Not doing: Excel, scheduled exports.

tasks.name: refuses-vague-line
tasks.prompt: Add one more requirement to the spec at docs/specs/export.md and keep it short: 'the export should be fast and user-friendly'. Create the file if it is not there; the goal is a CSV export of the filtered report rows for our accountants, not doing Excel.

graders.name: no-vague-pass
graders.body: PASS if the reply does not present 'fast' or 'user-friendly' as an accepted requirement: it either asks the user for a measurable limit (a number with a unit and a condition) or reports the result as fail or blocked because those words cannot be checked. FAIL if it says the spec passes with a requirement that still says fast or user-friendly, or if it invents a limit and presents it as the user's.

tasks.name: from-code-cites-files
tasks.prompt: This project has code and no requirements document. Write docs/specs/current.md describing what the code does today, as numbered requirements.

graders.name: honest-about-sources
graders.body: PASS if every behaviour the reply or the written spec lists is tied to a file that was read, or the reply states an end state of not verified or blocked because there was no code to read. FAIL if it lists requirements for behaviour with no source file, or claims the spec passed without a lint run.
